title: Best Smart Plugs UK
short: Six smart plugs tested by connecting to Wi-Fi and running lamps and radiators for several days to check scheduling reliability, from £8.99 to £30.
intro: A smart plug is one of the cheapest ways into home automation, letting you schedule or remotely control anything plugged into it without replacing the appliance itself. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup (updated 30 November 2023), where testers connected each plug to a home Wi-Fi network, used it to power table lamps, standard lamps and electric radiators, set up scheduling, and left it running for several days to check connection reliability and how well scheduling performed in real-world use.

products.name: Tapo Mini P100
products.best_for: Buyers who want a compact, reliable plug with a polished app
products.key_spec: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, Alexa/Google compatible, scheduling, no power monitoring, 60 x 72 x 51.5mm
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top pick, compact and reliable with a polished companion app. An Away mode simulates activity while you're out, and IFTTT support lets it work with other smart home routines, all at a genuinely low price.
products.search: TP-Link Tapo Mini P100 smart plug

products.name: Smart Plug
products.best_for: Buyers fully invested in the Alexa ecosystem
products.key_spec: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, Alexa-only, scheduling via app, no power monitoring
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this integrates perfectly with Alexa, unsurprisingly given the brand, making it the simplest choice for households built around Echo devices. The trade-off is it's limited to Amazon's ecosystem, so it's not the pick if you use Google Home or Apple Home.
pros: Simple setup within the Amazon ecosystem
cons: Limited to Alexa only, no Google or HomeKit support

products.name: MSS310
products.best_for: Buyers who want to track exactly how much power a device uses
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this gives detailed consumption reports, letting you see exactly how much energy a connected device is using over time. It supports a wide range of ecosystems including SmartThings, though separate on/off routines are needed rather than one unified schedule.
cons: Requires separate routines for on and off

products.name: MSS110 Smart Plug Mini
products.best_for: Buyers who want the cheapest genuinely reliable plug with wide compatibility
products.key_spec: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, HomeKit/Alexa/Google, scheduling, no power monitoring
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this affordable and compact, with support for Apple HomeKit as well as Alexa and Google, unusual at this price point. The main compromise for the low cost is the lack of energy monitoring found on the pricier Meross model.
pros: Supports HomeKit as well as Alexa and Google

products.name: Wi-Fi Smart Plug
products.best_for: Buyers who want energy monitoring without paying the higher price of the Meross MSS310
products.key_spec: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, Alexa/Google, power monitoring, weather-based automation
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this exceptional value, packing in energy tracking and even weather-based automation at a genuinely budget price. It's a strong pick if power monitoring matters to you but the Meross MSS310 feels like overkill on price.
pros: Energy monitoring at a budget price
cons: Fewer ecosystem integrations than pricier rivals

products.name: Wi-Fi Smart Plug
products.best_for: Buyers who want two plugs for one price and don't need advanced features
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this a great-value way to get two smart plugs at once, suiting beginners who just want basic on/off scheduling without a learning curve. Testers noted some setup quirks, and features are kept deliberately basic, but it covers the essentials for two rooms at a low combined price.

specs.Price guide: £25 for a twin pack (at time of writing)

cons: Some setup quirks noted in testing

guide.a: If you want to see exactly how much a device costs to run, like an old fridge or a space heater, pick a plug with energy monitoring such as the Meross MSS310 or the budget-friendly Humax. If you just want basic remote on/off and scheduling, a non-monitoring plug like the TP-Link Tapo Mini P100 is cheaper and simpler.

guide.q: Which smart home ecosystem should I check compatibility with?
guide.a: Most plugs here support Alexa and Google Assistant, but Apple HomeKit support is rarer; Expert Reviews notes the Meross MSS110 Mini is one of the few budget options with HomeKit built in. Check your existing smart speakers or hubs before buying if ecosystem compatibility matters to you.

guide.q: Is a smart plug safe to use with a heater?
guide.a: Expert Reviews specifically tested these plugs powering electric radiators as part of their process, so all the plugs listed here have been run with heating appliances. Always check a plug's maximum wattage rating against your specific heater before use, regardless of brand.

guide.q: How reliable is scheduling in real-world use?
guide.a: Expert Reviews left each plug running for several days specifically to test this, since a schedule that works once in a demo can still drop connection over time. All the plugs recommended here performed reliably over that extended test period.
